checks.ref:
command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
review="$reports/review-specs.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-specs stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: R1 (CRITICAL) is not real: the approved settings screenshots capture only the viewport (`locations_layout_e2e.steps.ts:76` calls `toHaveScreenshot(`${screenshotName}.png`)` without `fullPage`), and the baselines `__screenshots__/chromium/Approved-screenshots-of-the-settings-at-375-px-in-the-light-theme.png` and `...-1024-px-...` do not show the city data attribution at all; they end at the Language group and the offline notice. The attribution is the page's last line, so a changed dump date cannot alter these screenshots, and a city data refresh pull request will not fail them. The CRITICAL severity, the Fix (a `data-city-data-date` element replaced by a sample date in the screenshot step) and the Freshness note at line 42 ('That precedent matters for finding R1') rest on this false premise. Drop R1, or reduce it to the E2E text part only: no task names a literal date, and that part is already covered by R2's Fix.

Missed issue (WARNING): task 7.3 cannot be done as written. It re-approves the settings screenshots because 'FR12 puts a date into the city data attribution', asks to 'Read the 375 px PNGs and confirm the attribution line names the date of the city data', and requires `git status --short src/test/features/__screenshots__` to list exactly the 8 settings PNGs. The attribution is outside the viewport of every one of those PNGs, so nothing changes and the check fails. NFR-R1's 'The approved settings screenshots are re-approved once' has the same false premise. The report accepted task 7.3 instead of reporting it.

The Verdict ('Needs revision. Blocking: R1') is inconsistent once R1 falls: the blocking reason is a non-issue, and the real defect in task 7.3/NFR-R1 is not among the findings. The Summary counts (CRITICAL 1) must follow.
